subject: Why are these alternatives producing different scaled graphs

messages.author: 861fc89a46ceba40
messages.subject: Why are these alternatives producing different scaled graphs
parts:
I have drawn what I think should be the same density plots

1.

> p45Density<-ggplot(allbats,aes(x=allbats$count[allbats$species == "p45"]))
> print(p45Density + geom_density()+scale_x_continuous("Density of counts"))
Warning message:
Removed 9 rows containing missing values (stat_density).

2

> qplot(allbats$count[allbats$species == "p45"],geom="density", xlab="Density of Counts")
Warning message:
Removed 1 rows containing missing values (stat_density).

The former has a peak value of about 10-04, the latter 8-04

is the the first option removing all the rows with NAs even when there
isn't an NA in the variable I am interested in (p45), and the second
only removing the NA from the p45 variable

If this is the case, I wonder if someone could help with correct
syntax for ggplot2, as the qplot option is correct.

Many thanks,

Graham

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: Why are these alternatives producing different scaled graphs
parts:
Graham, 

I can't say I can tell what the problem is off the top of my head, but it seems like it's a problem specific to your dataset and how qplot() and ggplot() handle NAs. 

Something you could try is subsetting your data frame before handing it to qplot()/ggplot() and see if that changes anything. 

allbats.p45<-subset(allbats, species == "p45")

ggplot(allbats.p45 ,aes(x=allbats.p45$count)
+ geom_density()
+scale_x_continuous("Density of counts"))

#quartz() or windows() or x11() to open a new window for comparison's sake

qplot(allbats.p45$count
,geom="density"
,xlab="Density of Counts")

It'd be a lot easier to figure it out if we also had your dataset. If it's not too large use dput() and put it in this email thread or if it's larger dput() it into a text file or something (gmail cuts things off after a thousand or so lines). Change the variables and names if the data is sensitive. 

Brandon

parts:
Hi Graham:

Try to simplify the subsetting as I showed in my post. It's easier to follow, and it really, really works :) If that doesn't work, try the upgrades as Brandon suggested and try again. If ggplot() is removing 9 rows, it's using the entire data frame, not the p45 subset.

Here's the culprit:
p45Density<-ggplot(allbats, aes(x=allbats$count[allbats$species=="p45"]))

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
You're asking ggplot to read in the entire allbats data frame, but then subsetting x. In fact, it's the other way around: subset the data frame and then select the variable.

Hopefully, this solves the mystery :)

Dennis
